# Get-ZbxMaintenance

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the maintenance periods that cover planned work.

## SYNTAX

### All (Default)

## DESCRIPTION

A maintenance period suppresses problems, and optionally data collection, for hosts and host groups during planned work. The Get-ZbxMaintenance cmdlet reads them with maintenance.get: all of them up to -Limit, by name with -Name (* and ? are wildcards), by id with -Id or from the pipeline, or with the whole maintenance.get selection in -Filter. -Group, -Host and -Trigger narrow the result to the maintenance periods of the objects given, each a name, an id or a piped object. It writes ZabbixMaintenanceRecord objects, with their related objects when a -Select switch asks for them, or, with -CountOutput, the number of matches; it needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Get a maintenance by name

```powershell
Get-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Patch window' | Select-Object MaintenanceId, Name, MaintenanceType, ActiveSince, ActiveTill
```

-Name matches exactly; a * turns it into a search.

### Example 2: Find the maintenances a host or a group is assigned to

```powershell
Get-ZbxMaintenance -Host 'db-01' | Select-Object Name
Get-ZbxMaintenance -Group 'Web servers' | Select-Object Name
```

-Host (the alias of -HostReference) and -Group (maintenance.get's hostids, groupids) take names, ids or objects and match direct assignment only: a maintenance on 'Web servers' is not returned for -Host 'web-01'.

### Example 3: Show what a maintenance covers and when

```powershell
Get-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Patch window' -SelectHostGroups -SelectHosts -SelectTimePeriods | ForEach-Object {
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Name   = $_.Name
        Groups = $_.HostGroupsRead.Name -join ', '
        Hosts  = $_.Hosts.TechnicalName -join ', '
        Until  = $_.ActiveTill.UtcDateTime
    }
}
```

The -Select* switches add the related objects: the host groups (in HostGroupsRead), hosts and time periods.

### Example 4: List the maintenances that are active right now

```powershell
$now = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow
Get-ZbxMaintenance | Where-Object { $_.ActiveSince -le $now -and $_.ActiveTill -gt $now } | Select-Object Name, ActiveTill
```

ActiveSince/ActiveTill are times; compare them with the current time. (A maintenance's periods decide when inside that range the hosts are actually in maintenance.)
